chunks: From him, from Abī Aḥmad, from one whom he mentioned, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: The muḥrim strikes game and then offers compensation for it—may he eat it, or should he discard it? He said: Then there would be another compensation upon him. I said: So what should he do with it? He said: He should bury it.

Were it not that it takes the ruling of carrion, according to what the earlier reports contain, he would not have ordered him to bury it; rather, he would have ordered him to feed it to those who are not in iḥrām.

key_terms.الصَّيْدَ: game animal hunted in the wild
key_terms.الْمَيْتَةِ: carrion, an unslaughtered dead animal with legal impurity of use for eating
key_terms.الْمُحِلِّينَ: those not in the state of iḥrām
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: a person in the state of iḥrām for hajj or ʿumrah
key_terms.فَيَفْدِيهِ: then he offers expiation or compensation for it
key_terms.يَدْفِنُهُ: he buries it and does not use it

ai.seo_question: What should a muḥrim do with hunted game after paying the expiation?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning game killed by a muḥrim during iḥrām. Even if compensation is due, the animal is not to be eaten or given for consumption; rather, it is to be buried, indicating that it takes the ruling of carrion in this context.
